newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa FSB signs deal with U.S. supervisory body.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa FSB signs deal with U.S. supervisory body.

text.p: South Africa's Financial Services Board (FSB) on Tuesday signed a joint information, co-operation and consultation communique with the United States' Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).
The FSB said in a statement the joint agreement was a product of extensive consultation between the two parties.

"It is intended to establish arrangements for the exchange of information for investigatory, supervisory and surveillance purposes to assist one another in discharging its regulatory duties," it said.
The information exchange would help enhance fair dealing on the futures and options markets by increased effectiveness of regulation and in the supervision of cross-border transactions.
"The signing of the joint communique underscores South Africa's increasing role in the global financial markets," said FSB executive officer Rick Cottrell.
CFTC representative John Tull said the agreement was part of the U.S. supervisory authority's commitment to information sharing with international authorities.

The FSB already has similar arrangements with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission, the United Kingdom Securities and Investments Board and the Securities and Futures Commission of Taiwan.
